subject: Discovery recap - Moneta - p95 latency & concurrency requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@moneta.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@moneta.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap - Moneta - p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please call out anything I missed.

Pain points (what you told us):
- Customer-facing chat experiences are regularly violating your UX SLOs during peak hours (not just tail cases). Current p95 generation latency ~800–1200ms for typical queries.
- Streaming experience is inconsistent: first-byte for streaming responses can be 300–600ms and partial token cadence is bursty, which harms perceived responsiveness.
- Concurrency spikes (trading hours) cause queuing; you see request fan-in up to ~120–150 concurrent requests hitting the model, with throughput cliffs and retries.
- Current stack: An internal model stack on AWS EKS using g5dn-like instances behind a custom autoscaler. No prefix/KV cache and limited request-level batching logic.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- p95 end-to-end generation latency consistently <= 300ms for single-turn queries (goal).
- Streaming first-byte under 100ms, and steady partial-token cadence (every 50–150ms) for the interactive experience.
- Handle sustained 100–150 concurrent active sessions without client-side queuing or >2% error rate.
- No regression in result quality vs current model (we’ll validate with your eval prompts).

What Redwood can help with / proposed approach:
- Quick perf characterization (we’ll run a lightweight traffic replay against a mirrored model endpoint to reproduce p95 and concurrency behavior).
- Observability: token-level latency breakdowns (kernel / inference / network) and per-request KV/cache hit rates.
- Optimization levers: batching profiles, prefix/KV caching, quantization recommendations, and streaming plumbing to reduce first-byte.
- PoC plan: 2-week focused lab where we validate p95 and streaming on a small sample workload, then propose Dedicated sizing or routing policies for production.

Immediate next steps (to confirm):
1) Technical deep-dive (60 min) with your infra team + our inference engineer (Aditya) — propose Fri Apr 30, 10:00am PT.
2) You share a small representative dataset / subset of queries (sensitive data can be redacted) + expected success prompts.
3) We’ll schedule a load window for a controlled replay and send a stub performance report (pdf) within 48 hours of replay.

Attachments: redwood_prod_perf_stub.pdf (sample report format we’ll produce after the replay)

Thanks — I’ll wait for availability for the deep-dive and the sample queries.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@moneta.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@moneta.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - Moneta - p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Thanks Marissa — this looks right and captures the key points. A few clarifications / notes from our side: 

- The 800–1200ms p95 is for our current sync path; we do have an async streaming path in prod but it’s only used for long-form responses and is inconsistent because of our middleware.
- Concurrency: 120–150 is typical during spikes, but we’d like headroom to 200 for peak events.
- Token sizes: 90% of queries are under 300 tokens; ~10% are long (>1k tokens) that we can route differently.
- Security: we need to validate KMS integration and audit logs before any Private/Dedicated work.

Fri Apr 30 at 10am PT works for the deep-dive — Priya and I will be on the call. Can Aditya confirm?

Also: attaching a short sample query set (we’ll drop the payloads into the Drive folder you shared).

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Lead Platform Engineer, Moneta
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@moneta.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - Moneta - p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Hi Daniel / Marissa —

Thanks — confirmed for Fri Apr 30, 10:00am PT. I’ll bring the inference engineer who owns our streaming and batching stack. A few prep notes so we can make the deep-dive productive: 

1) Please share a representative set of request traces (anonymized) and an example long request. If you can include the client-side timestamps (request send / first-byte / final-byte) that will help us map the latency breakdown.
2) If possible, provide a lightweight topology diagram of your current infra (how requests route, where autoscaler sits, networking).
3) For the replay: we prefer a subset of 500–2,000 requests that mirror peak QPS patterns; we’ll coordinate timing to avoid impacting prod.

Initial hypotheses from your description: 
- Missing prefix/KV cache and suboptimal batching likely explain most of the p95 gap for short queries.
- Streaming first-byte issues could be middleware buffering or kernel scheduling starved under concurrent loads.
- Autoscaler settings might be too reactive for short, high-QPS bursts — we’ll look at warm capacity and burst pools.

I’ll prepare an agenda and a minimal data checklist and drop it into the Drive link you mentioned.

See you Fri.
Aditya Rao
Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@moneta.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@moneta.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap - Moneta - p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Perfect — thanks all. We’ll: 
- Drop the anonymized traces and short topology doc into the Drive by EOD Thu.
- Confirm the 500–2,000 request window and preferred times for the replay in the agenda (we prefer after-hours, 10pm–2am PT for less user impact).
- Priya will add a short security requirements doc re: KMS + retention.

Looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Daniel
